reading.maqta: Maqta — the closing couplet bearing the poet’s pen name

gloss.GHAZAL: Ghazal: a lyric poem of couplets (beyts) on a single rhyme.
gloss.MASNAVI: Masnavi: a long poem in self-rhyming couplets, usually an epic or a tale.
gloss.RUBAI: Rubai: a philosophical quatrain; lines one, two and four rhyme.
gloss.QASIDA: Qasida: a long, formal poem of praise or counsel.
gloss.MURABBA: Murabba: a poem in four-line stanzas.

reading.gloss_maqta: The closing couplet is the maqta: there the poet signs with a pen name.
reading.gloss_source: Dictionary of Arabic and Persian Words, Baku, 2005

tree.title: Literature tree
tree.lead: All of Azerbaijani literature from Dədə Qorqud to today on one tree: eras, branches, authors. Leaves fill in as you read; dashed ones are not on the site yet.
tree.guest_title: Watch the tree fill as you read
tree.guest_text: Sign in and every work you finish fills its author’s ring, so you can see which eras you have not opened yet.
tree.rings_me: Each band is an era: its width follows how much the site holds, the coloured part is how much of it you have read.
tree.rings_guest: Each band is an era; the coloured part is how much of it the site already holds.
tree.era_missing: {n, plural, one {# author or text still missing} other {# authors or texts still missing}}
tree.suggest_text: If you know an author or work that is not on the tree, or where to find an edition or scan of it, tell us and we will add it.
tree.footnote: Authors on the site are placed automatically; the list of missing ones is an editorial selection, not a full bibliography. Dates for the early eras are approximate.
